title: My students came up with a game idea, and we used AI to help bring it to life
author: Regular_Room4082
selftext:
Hey everyone! I wanted to share a project that my engineering class and I have been working on called UpTrade.

How it works is you start with a red paperclip and try to trade your way up to a car before time runs out. You make different deals, visit different locations, find rare items, and hope you don’t get stuck with a bad trade including getting scammed!

My favorite part of this project isn't even the game itself. It's how it came together.

The ideas came from our middle school students. They shared things they thought would be cool, features they wanted, and ideas for how the game should work. Then, as an engineering class, we talked through those ideas, figured out what was possible, tested things, and worked to turn their thoughts into an actual game.

We used Claude and ChatGPT to help us with the coding, fixing errors, and figuring out how to make different features work. There were definitely frustrating moments when things broke and we had to try again, but that was part of the process too.

I think it’s pretty cool that students can come up with an idea and actually get to see it become something people can play. AI helped us with the technical side, but the creativity and ideas that shaped the game came from the students. Seeing everyone contribute and watching the project come together has been a really rewarding experience.

We're still working on improving it, but we're excited to finally share it and see what people think!

🎮 **You can play UpTrade here:** [https://wkeytherapy.itch.io/uptrade](https://wkeytherapy.itch.io/uptrade)

One other thing: the game is free to play, and donations are completely optional. If anyone does choose to donate, **all donations will go toward our engineering class and TSA (Technology Student Association)** to help support our students and future projects. There's absolutely no pressure to donate — even just trying the game or sharing it means a lot.

If you get a chance to play, let us know what you think! We'd love to hear what works, what could be better, or what ideas you have.

Thanks for checking out our little project! ❤️
